_note: Human sign-off 2026-09-01 (epic #636 gate; maintainer sign-off comment on #636). This is the machine-readable single source of truth for per-agent-type rate limits, circuit breakers, and the org-wide Claude token-budget breaker. Decision record: docs/initiatives/agent-rate-limits-adr.md (#637). The per-agent-type limits and consecutive-failure breakers are now CONSUMED at dispatch time by scripts/agent-rate-limit-gate.sh (Phase 4, #640): initiative-driver ENFORCES, every other agent type runs log-only. org_wide.token_budget is now wired into that same dispatch path but DISARMED (#1155): scripts/agent-rate-limit-gate.sh consults the session + weekly_all windows, yet the consultation is gated on AGENT_TOKEN_BUDGET_ENABLED which stays unset, and org_wide.token_budget.limits.weekly_all.enabled stays false — so the breaker is inert (byte-identical to per-agent-only behaviour). Arming it (setting the flag with the private telemetry seam, and flipping weekly_all.enabled for the glide-path half) is a separate, deliberately-out-of-scope change (#994). Consumers read values from this single file, never hardcoded.

dev-lead._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §6). max_concurrent_runs is the global type cap on top of the existing per-issue/per-PR lanes; cooldown is the quiet interval between issue pickups; daily_run_budget bounds runs per rolling 24h. Whether the concurrency cap is global vs per-repo is deferred to sign-off.

compliance-audit._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §6). Already single-lane, non-cancelling on a weekly cron; cooldown_minutes is 0 (not applicable to a weekly run — encoded as 0, not a faked positive value). daily_run_budget of 1 reflects the weekly cadence.

feature-ideation._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §6). Already single-lane, non-cancelling on a weekly cron; cooldown_minutes is 0 (not applicable to a weekly run). daily_run_budget of 1 reflects the weekly cadence.

initiative-driver._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §6). Runs no LLM itself (pure-bash dispatcher); its cost is the dev-lead fan-out it triggers, so daily_run_budget here is a DISPATCHES/day bound (ADR §3) — the concrete key that keeps a single epic from flooding dev-lead. cooldown_minutes targets the close-event + schedule double-fire race (#443).

token_budget._note: Org-wide Claude subscription token-budget breaker (ADR §7). INERT pending human sign-off; no workflow reads it (AC #3). Telemetry source of record is the OAuth usage endpoint (ADR §4.1), read privately (ADR §8.2) — this public file holds only the thresholds/policy. The session (5-hour) and weekly_all (7-day) windows are FIXED windows with an authoritative resets_at (ADR §4.1); within a window percent is monotonically non-decreasing and only the reset lowers it. There is deliberately NO percentage resume mark — under a fixed window a downward dip cannot occur, so such a mark would be unreachable (ADR §7). Only account-wide windows are pause-worthy; weekly_scoped (per-model) exhaustion is handled by the engine's model-fallback chain, never a fleet pause (ADR §2.5).
token_budget._claude_priority_note: PROPOSAL (ADR §7). On budget recovery, Claude-backed agents (dev-lead, feature-ideation, and the Claude phase of compliance-audit) are prioritized so the recovering budget clears the backlog first; initiative-driver dispatch resumes after the direct Claude consumers.

session._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §7). Pause new agentic dispatch when the 5-hour subscription budget reaches pause_threshold_pct (default 90%). Closes only at the window's resets_at (fixed window) — no intermediate half-open state, no resume percentage.

weekly_all._note: PROPOSAL (ADR §7; Phase 6 #994). Glide-path breaker: pause when percent >= clamp(ceiling_pct - (reserve_pct_per_day * days_until_reset), floor_pct, ceiling_pct). With reserve_pct_per_day=2, ceiling_pct=100, floor_pct=86 the schedule is 100% on reset day .. 86% just after a reset — the whole schedule is expressible from these keys, nothing is hardcoded. INERT: enabled=false keeps the breaker off (a maintainer arms it in config), independent of the AGENT_TOKEN_BUDGET_ENABLED integration flag. The threshold RISES as the reset approaches, so the breaker can close before resets_at because the threshold moved past a static (monotonic) percent — never because utilization fell; there is deliberately no percentage resume mark. days_until_reset derives from the authoritative resets_at (ADR §4.1) with partial days rounded UP, not a hardcoded weekday. floor_pct is the 'don't spend the whole week on day one' guard; ceiling_pct is the reset-day cap where the budget is minutes from refilling.

weekly_scoped._note: Per-model exhaustion. Never pause-worthy (ADR §2.5): handled by the engine's model-fallback chain (swap models), not a fleet pause.

_exempt_note: Actors/labels whose agent runs must never be blocked or deferred by the rate limits — the SAME set as standards/pr-limits.json so one policy governs both gates. dependabot[bot] is already bounded per-ecosystem by its own open-pull-requests-limit; OrganizationAdmin / @petry-projects/org-leads are human break-glass and maintainer traffic; dependabot-automerge-petry operates on existing PRs; security-labeled work is urgent and bypasses any throttle.
